g.text: Two devices are using the same IP address.
We found 1 problem affecting your network, and no sign of an attack. This looks like an ordinary fault
Two devices are using the same IP address
192.168.1.23 is being used by two devices at once: 00:80:92:5e:31:7a and f4:5c:89:aa:10:99 (6 claims from
Every device on a network needs its own IP address. When two devices are given the same
one, they keep 'stealing' it from each other, so both lose their connection randomly. This usually happens
when someone sets a fixed (static) IP that the DHCP server also hands out, or two devices were configured
by hand with the same number.
Like two houses on the same street with the same house number: the post goes to one or the other at
A static IP address that overlaps with another device or with the DHCP pool
1. Find both devices: look up 00:80:92:5e:31:7a and f4:5c:89:aa:10:99 in the router's client list or
2. On the device with the fixed address, switch to automatic (DHCP): Windows
then set 'Obtain an IP address automatically'; Linux
3. If you need static addresses, pick them outside the DHCP range, or use DHCP reservations on the
(or reconnect Wi-Fi) on the affected devices.
Why we think it's a misconfiguration
A device probed 192.168.1.23 before using it (RFC 5227 duplicate-address check), which is normal
Both MACs send their own normal traffic from 192.168.1.23: two real devices think the address is
The disputed address 192.168.1.23 is not the router's
Not someone is impersonating 192.168.1.23 (arp spoofing / man-in-the-middle): Nothing in the traffic
pointed to an attack. The stronger evidence: A device probed 192.168.1.23 before using it (RFC 5227
duplicate-address check), which is normal boot behaviour; Both MACs send their own normal traffic from
192.168.1.23: two real devices think the address is theirs.
